nodes.label: User (browser or API client)
nodes.summary: Creates short links (write) and follows them (read, ~100x more often).

nodes.label: CDN / edge
nodes.summary: Serves hot redirects from the edge and collapses simultaneous misses for one link into a single origin request.
nodes.details: Collapsed forwarding is a documented Squid feature `[CONFIRMED]`. Using it for a viral short link is the design application `[INDUSTRY PATTERN]`.

nodes.label: Load balancer
nodes.summary: Spreads traffic across stateless service instances. Read and write paths run on separate fleets so redirects never starve shortening.

nodes.label: Shorten service
nodes.summary: Validates the long URL, enforces 1:1 / custom aliases, asks the KGS for a key and writes the mapping.

nodes.label: Redirect service
nodes.summary: Looks up short→long and answers 301 or 302. 301 is heuristically cacheable by browsers, 302 is not.
nodes.details: Status-code semantics are `[CONFIRMED]` in RFC 9110 §15.4: 301 is heuristically cacheable, 307 MUST NOT change the method. Choosing 301 vs 302 is a product trade-off between cache efficiency and click analytics.

nodes.label: Key generation service
nodes.summary: Hands out unique keys from an in-memory leased counter range, base62-encoded to 7 characters (3.5 trillion keys).
nodes.details: Losing an in-memory range on a crash only wastes IDs. Raw counters are predictable, so scramble them (random bits, shuffled ranges or a bijective permutation) if guessability matters.

nodes.label: Token range service
nodes.summary: Strongly consistent store (ZooKeeper or DynamoDB with conditional writes) that leases non-overlapping counter ranges to KGS instances.

nodes.label: Bloom filters
nodes.summary: Answers "definitely not seen" cheaply: short-URL filter returns 404 without hitting cache or DB. Long-URL filter shortcuts the 1:1 check. False positives, never false negatives.
nodes.details: Standard Bloom filters cannot delete, so expired links still answer "maybe" and fall through to the lookup.

nodes.label: Redis cache
nodes.summary: Cache-aside, LRU, ~1 day TTL, partitioned by short URL. Cache on the second access to avoid thrashing on one-hit links.

nodes.label: URL store (NoSQL KV)
nodes.summary: short_url → long_url + metadata. Partitioned by short URL via consistent hashing (DynamoDB / Cassandra class).
nodes.details: Capacity (assumed 100M writes/day, 5 yrs, ~2.5 KB/record): ~1k writes/s, ~100k reads/s, ~456 TB before replication.

nodes.label: Inverted index
nodes.summary: long_url → short_url, partitioned by long URL. Only needed when the same long URL must map to the same short URL (1:1), which most real products skip.

nodes.label: Kafka (click events)
nodes.summary: The redirect service emits a click event; analytics consumes it asynchronously so a slow warehouse never delays a redirect.

nodes.label: Analytics warehouse
nodes.summary: Batch store (HDFS / warehouse) for non-real-time click counts, referrers and geo.

steps.caption: The browser requests the short URL. Popular redirects are answered at the edge.
On an edge miss the request goes to the origin. Simultaneous misses for the same link are collapsed into one.
The load balancer routes it to a stateless redirect instance.
A Bloom filter rejects keys that were never created, so scans never reach the cache or database.
Cache-aside lookup in Redis.
On a cache miss the value is read from the URL store, then cached.
A click event is emitted asynchronously. The 301/302 response does not wait for it.
Analytics consumes the events in batches, off the hot path.
The client submits the long URL (and optionally an alias and expiry).
A shorten-service instance takes the request.
If 1:1 is required, a Bloom filter says whether this long URL was definitely never seen.
On a "maybe", the inverted index confirms whether a short URL already exists. A lock on the long URL prevents concurrent duplicates.
Otherwise ask the key generation service for a key from its in-memory range.
Only when its range is exhausted does the KGS lease a new non-overlapping range from the consistent store.
The mapping is written to the URL store (and the inverted index when 1:1 is on).
A flood of requests for one short link arrives. The CDN answers repeats from the edge.
Concurrent misses are collapsed into a single origin request (request coalescing, a standard technique).
The origin looks the key up in the cache.
At most one read reaches the URL store.
Click events go to a stream asynchronously, so analytics never slow the redirect.
A key generator serves keys from an in-memory range it leased earlier.
After a crash, a replacement leases a new non-overlapping range. The unused part of the old range is wasted, which is acceptable out of 3.5 trillion keys.
Writes continue with no collision, because ranges never overlap.
